$empty: ⚠️ THIS FILE IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT (2026-08-20). THE APP COMES EMPTY. Not 'empty of workflows' — empty. No services, no engines, no workflows, no styles, no media. A fresh install can be asked for nothing at all, and every single thing it can eventually do arrived because somebody put it there: ⤓ from the library at xoko.lat, or ＋ by hand on the 🔌 page. An app that came with a curated shelf would be an app whose shelf is ours instead of yours.
$where-the-services-went: Six rows lived here until today — draw-things-grpc, comfyui, rembg, claude-code, ollama, cloud-text — on the argument that a service row is FORMAT rather than content, because it names a transport this build ships code for. The argument was half right and the conclusion was wrong: what this build can SPEAK is code (src/inference/presets.ts, src/inference/cli/brains.ts, and the parser that refuses anything else), while what you have actually pointed it at is a choice, and a choice belongs to you. Shipping the rows meant a cleared install still showed six services, four of them for software the user may not own, and one of them answering — which then reported nine checkpoints. That is not an empty app.
$so-how-does-anything-get-here: ＋ add a service on the 🔌 page, which offers SERVICE_PRESETS — the transports this build knows how to speak, in code, where a downloaded payload can never reach them (src/library/payload.ts). Picking one writes a row into <app data>/registries/inference.json, which is YOUR layer. The security property the shipped rows were defending is untouched: the whitelist was never this file, it was the parser and the preset list.
$comment: Shipped INFERENCE registry — layer 1 of 2, and deliberately carrying nothing. Your own rows live at <app data>/registries/inference.json. If a row ever does ship again it merges field by field with yours, `engines` per file and `workflows` per slug (src/inference/registry.ts).
